D.t: John Hickenlooper leads by 17.5 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 496,428 votes; a one point swing is about 14,159 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +8.8 and D +25.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 217,824 votes; Boulder, a projected net 113,161 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 86,083 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +6.8, 11.9% of the vote; Douglas, R +4.2, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +3.1, 2.7% of the vote; Garfield, D +8.9, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, John Hickenlooper runs furthest behind in Mesa, Weld, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 54 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Large counties, 79% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.93 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 58 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points.
The forecast's worst groups for John Hickenlooper: Immigration voters 20 to 78, Small counties 45 to 52, Midsize counties 48 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.1M cash against $28K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
